text:
julie_acme: Hey, we're seeing a weird one — ran a long streaming chat session from our app but our Credits balance didn't change at all. Account ACME-42. Request id: req_0a1b2c3d. SDK: sdk-js v2.3.1. Logged ~18k generated tokens according to client. Can someone look? :confused:

alex_support: thanks julie — sorry that's annoying. Can you paste the exact request payload (headers + body) you used for the stream and the finalization call? Also confirm whether you call any finalize/close event on the stream.

julie_acme: minimal repro below. We open a streaming chat, send messages, then call finish() on the SDK. Example curl we use to emulate:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-chat-1","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"long prompt..."}]}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat.create
# then client sends stream events over websocket and calls client.finish() which maps to /chat.finalize
```

alex_support: got it. Do you have the server-side /chat.finalize request id? The billing pipeline only counts tokens when the finalize event is received. If finalize never reached us, it explains zero debit.

julie_acme: we log a success for finish() — client shows 200. The client prints a header x-request-id:req_0a1b2c3d on the initial create; finalize shows x-request-id:req_0a1b2c3d-finalize. I can attach logs.

maya_eng: pinging infra — can you paste the finalize HTTP exchange (status, headers)? If client sees 200 but we never received the finalize webhook, there could be a retry path or proxy swallowed the body. Also need server logs around req_0a1b2c3d-finalize.

jordan_sre: I pulled logs for req_0a1b2c3d and I see chat.create and multiple chunk events, but I do NOT see a chat.finalize event in our ingress for that session between 2025-11-05T10:12:00Z and 2025-11-05T10:20:00Z. The client-side header 'finalize' request seems to have 200 in the SDK, but upstream returned 204 with no body and no finalize record. Could be a proxy returning 204 early. :eyes:

emma_billing: from billing ledger side, there are no debit entries for ACME-42 for that timeframe. Metering keys are tied to finalize events. No post-facto debits observed.

julie_acme: hmm — our SRE says the app server got 200 on finalize. Attaching excerpt:

```
[APP] POST /chat/finalize -> 200 OK
[APP] resp-headers: x-proxy-status: ok, content-length: 0
[APP] client-sdk: finalize resolved
```

alex_support: that header x-proxy-status looks custom. Can you try bypassing the proxy (call Redwood API directly from a small curl from your laptop) and reproduce? If direct finalize reaches us, proxy is the cause.

julie_acme: ok will test direct now.

(10m later)

julie_acme: Quick update — calling finalize directly from my laptop to https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat.finalize with the same payload returns 204 and still no debit. Request IDs: req_0a1b2c3d-finalize-direct.

maya_eng: thanks — posting debug info: on ingestion we expect either 200/202 with a finalize event body; a 204 with no body gets treated as 'no finalize' by the metering pipeline. It looks like our server currently needs a non-empty finalize event to trigger token accounting. We're seeing 204 responses for some finalize paths which the meter ignores.

alex_support: TL;DR: finalize is reaching endpoints but empty 204s are not being counted. Two possible causes: 1) client is sending finalize but not including final token counts in the body (so 204 emitted), or 2) server path returns 204 before commit. We'll need a quick repro so eng can patch to accept 204 as finalize or ensure finalize returns a body.

emma_billing: policy note — if we accept 204 as finalize, we must ensure idempotency and not double-charge on retries. Billing team onboard for design review.

jordan_sre: action: I collected the ingress traces for req_0a1b2c3d-finalize-direct -> trace_id trace-77f. Attaching mini-trace snippet:

```
ingress -> auth -> gateway (returned 204 early) -> no finalize payload forwarded to metering -> ack to client
```

maya_eng: root cause hypothesis: an early response path in gateway for streaming sessions returns 204 for finalize when client uses empty body; metering expects a finalize payload (token delta). Fix options: accept 204 w/ lookup of session KV cache to compute tokens OR require client to include finalize body with totals.

alex_support: julie — could you try updating SDK to v2.4.0-rc which includes a change to always include finalize metadata in the body? Quick test: upgrade to rc and re-run, then paste new request ids.

julie_acme: will try and report back. ETA ~1h.

billing-bot: Ticket created: #SUP-3247 — "ACME-42: streaming sessions showing zero debit due to empty finalize 204 path". Assigned to maya_eng + jordan_sre.

(1h later)

julie_acme: Tested with sdk-js v2.4.0-rc, re-ran the same flow. New create req: req_0b9c8d7e, finalize req: req_0b9c8d7e-finalize. This time the finalize included body: {"generated_tokens":18342,"prompt_tokens":1240}. We see ledger entries created and balance decreased accordingly. :thumbsup:

emma_billing: verified ledger entries for ACME-42 at 2025-11-05T11:45:00Z — debits match tokens reported. We'll retroactively credit any impacted sessions if needed after triage.

maya_eng: root cause confirmed: gateway treated empty finalize as a 204 ack and did not forward session totals. Plan: patch gateway to accept an empty finalize by fetching KV cache totals OR force non-empty finalize bodies. Short-term fix: require SDKs to send finalize metadata (we pushed rc). Long-term: gateway will be updated to forward finalize regardless. Rolling patch ETA: 48h.

julie_acme: thanks everyone — appreciate fast help. We'll roll sdk upgrade to prod. Please keep me posted on any retroactive credits.

alex_support: noted — we'll follow up in ticket SUP-3247 once gateway patch is live. For now closing Slack thread; keeping ticket open. :white_check_mark:
